content:
One year into Tamaulipas's new court system, the woman running it says criminal cases are moving dramatically faster: hearings that used to be scheduled up to four months out are now happening in about 15 days. That was the headline Tuesday when Magistrada Presidenta Tania Gisela Contreras López delivered her first report at the head of the state's new Poder Judicial, according to InfoExprés.

The report, presented at 11 a.m. in the Poder Judicial auditorium in Ciudad Victoria with Gov. Américo Villarreal Anaya in attendance, is one of the first accountability exercises for a court system that took office on October 1, 2025. Contreras López told the audience the wait-time reductions come from a deliberate push against the backlog: the judiciary swore in 30 new court secretaries last week and plans to add 60 more support staff in November, while running hearing rooms in evening hours and on weekends, according to advance coverage in Informativo Victoria.

The gains are not limited to criminal matters. Civil cases that once took around three weeks to resolve are now averaging about a week, and the judiciary reports progress in labor and family matters as well. Contreras López also pointed to a new digital platform, "Consulta tu expediente," with roughly 700 records registered, that lets Tamaulipas residents track their cases from a phone without an intermediary — and to a crime-incidence diagnostic being built with the Universidad Autónoma de Tamaulipas.

Looking ahead, the judiciary plans to launch oral proceedings in civil and family matters starting in April 2027, a shift officials say will make justice more humane and closer to the people.

What to watch: advance coverage of Tuesday's report said personnel changes — including the removal of 12 officials — were also expected to be addressed. For families in Nuevo Laredo, the question is whether the 15-day promise holds in the border courts as well as in the capital, and whether the new hires and evening dockets translate into cases actually resolved — not just scheduled. This is exactly the kind of pledge a watchdog keeps on file.

Sources:

  • InfoExprés
  • Informativo Victoria

— Waldo Wolf, Nuevo Laredo Correspondent, Webb Watch 956

title: Tamaulipas Courts Cut Criminal Hearing Waits From 4 Months to 15 Days, Top Judge Reports
